text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Patient

text:
Given your complex history and current symptoms of ataxia, could you tell me if you have a known history of autoimmune disorders, infections like Lyme disease, or any prior exposure to heavy metals like mercury?

REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Panel (ANA, ESR, CRP), Infectious Disease Serology, and Heavy Metal Toxicity Screen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your autoimmune, infectious, and toxicity screens are normal, I need to rule out structural spinal cord issues next. Have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or hands, and have you been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis or a similar condition?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical and Thoracic Spine with contrast
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain results

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML); T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without contrast enhancement in the brain, combined with your ataxia, are classic for this JC virus-associated opportunistic infection, often seen in patients with significant immunosuppression.
